VegetationLibrary__Register__Meta.Meta__Description: The single source of truth for the vegetation library's numbering: the namespace, the collections, each collection's types and the blocks of numbers they own. The build util and the app read it; nothing else decides a number.
VegetationLibrary__Register__Meta.Meta__WhyThisForm: PainterlyNPR's register, with its own namespacer: VVL_07_1001 sits beside NPR_07_1001, and the collection and block numbers mean the same in both, so a shrub is 07_10xx in either library. Adam, 30-Oct-2026, of NPR: "asset subfolder in numbered series in my style to keep things organised and unique asset ID codes".

VegetationLibrary__Register__Numbering.Numbering__NamespaceNote: ValeVision Linework: every asset Id starts VVL_, so an Id is unique beside NPR_ and the component library's own codes
VegetationLibrary__Register__Numbering.Numbering__IdPatternNote: VVL_CC_TTFI. CC the collection, 05 to 80. TT the type's block. F the family, 0 to 9. I the item, 1 to 9. An I of 0 is a family's base and is never an asset
VegetationLibrary__Register__Numbering.Numbering__RetiredIdsNote: A retired Id is never reused: projects may hold a pinned copy of it for ever. List it here when its asset's Meta__Status becomes Retired

VegetationLibrary__Register__Naming.Naming__AssetFileNote: One file per asset, in its collection's folder: VVL_07_1001__Shrubs__RoundedShrub__Var-01__.json. No picture files and no SKP slot: cards are drawn live by the code that draws the scene
VegetationLibrary__Register__Naming.Naming__MaxRelativePathNote: Characters from this library's root, as NPR's: SketchUp's Ruby cannot open a path over 259, and Cloud Sync will read these from Stage 9
